Visualization Gallery

Source: vignettes/visualization-gallery.Rmd
visualization-gallery.Rmd

Overview

mortensor provides a rich set of ggplot2-based visualisations for every stage of the mortality forecasting pipeline. All plot functions either use S3 plot() methods (dispatched by object class and type argument) or standalone plot_*() functions for specialised diagnostics.

This vignette is a complete visual reference for every plot type.

Setup 

library(mortensor)
data(example_mortality)

# Run the full pipeline to generate objects for all plot types
sm  <- smooth_mortality(example_mortality, method = "gam",
                        covid_years = c(2020L, 2021L))
cal <- calibrate(sm, holdout_frac = 0.2, ensemble = TRUE)
fc  <- forecast(cal, h = 10)
fc  <- add_pi(fc, n_sim = 500, method = "bootstrap")
fc_1yr <- disaggregate(fc, target_ages = 30:100,
                       method = "natural_gompertz")

1. Observed data plots (plot.mort_data)

The plot() method for mort_data supports three visualisation types.

Heatmap

A Lexis-style heatmap of log(mx)\log(m_x) across age groups and years:

plot(example_mortality, type = "heatmap", group = 1)
  • x-axis: Calendar year
  • y-axis: Age group
  • Fill: log(mx)\log(m_x), with gradient from low (blue) to high (red)
  • Useful for spotting period effects (e.g. COVID), cohort effects, and data quality issues

Age profile

Age-specific mortality rates for selected years:

plot(example_mortality, type = "age_profile", group = 1)
  • x-axis: Age group
  • y-axis: log(mx)\log(m_x)
  • Colour: Year
  • Useful for checking the age gradient and identifying crossing patterns

Trend

Time series of age-averaged mortality:

plot(example_mortality, type = "trend", group = 1)
  • x-axis: Year
  • y-axis: Mean log(mx)\log(m_x) across ages
  • Useful for assessing the overall decline rate and identifying shocks

2. Calibration plot (plot.mort_calibration)

Model comparison bar chart 

plot(cal)
  • x-axis: Model name
  • y-axis: MASE (combined)
  • Colour: Model family (Tucker, demographic, time-series)
  • Horizontal line at MASE = 1 (naive baseline)
  • Ensemble members highlighted

This is the key visual for communicating model selection results.

3. Forecast plots (plot.mort_forecast)

The plot() method for mort_forecast supports eight visualisation types. All types that show groups automatically use the metadata from fc$groups (e.g. sex, quintile). By default the last group column maps to colour and earlier columns to facets. Override with facet_by and color_by.

Prediction interval fan chart 

plot(fc, type = "pi")
  • x-axis: Year (training + forecast)
  • y-axis: log(mx)\log(m_x)
  • Fan: 95% PI ribbon (shaded) with median line
  • Points: Observed (training) data
  • Faceted by age group (and group label when multiple groups)
  • The most important diagnostic: do PIs capture the data-generating process?

Trends with PI envelope 

plot(fc, type = "trends")
  • Age-averaged log(mx)\log(m_x) across time
  • Observed dots + fitted solid line (with 95% GAM Bayesian CI ribbon when available) + forecast dashed line with PI ribbon
  • Colour by group variable, faceted by remaining group variables
  • Vertical dotted line marks forecast start
  • Useful for checking that forecast trajectories are plausible

Trends by age group 

plot(fc, type = "trends_by_age")
  • Same as "trends" but faceted by representative age groups (40–44, 50–54, 60–64, 70–74, 80–84, 90+)
  • Uses facet_grid(age_group ~ facet_by) when a facet variable is set
  • Useful for checking age-specific forecast behaviour

Controlling group aesthetics 

# Override auto-detected facet/colour mapping
plot(fc, type = "trends", facet_by = "sex", color_by = "quintile")
plot(fc, type = "trends_by_age", facet_by = "sex", color_by = "quintile")

Age profiles 

plot(fc, type = "age")
  • Age profiles for the final forecast year
  • Compared against the last observed year
  • Shows whether the age gradient is preserved in the forecast

Residuals 

plot(fc, type = "residuals")
  • Heatmap of in-sample residuals: log(m̂x)−log(mx)\log(\hat{m}_x) - \log(m_x)
  • Blue: overprediction, Red: underprediction
  • Structured residuals indicate model misspecification
  • Faceted by group metadata

Smoothing comparison 

plot(fc, type = "smoothing")
  • Time-series view: observed dots + smoothed lines
  • 95% GAM Bayesian credible interval ribbon (when GAM fits are available)
  • Colour by group variable, faceted by remaining group variables
  • Useful for assessing the degree and quality of smoothing

Tucker3 components 

plot(fc, type = "components")
  • The B-mode temporal components from Tucker3 decomposition
  • Training period (points) and forecast extrapolation (line + CI)
  • Component 1 = dominant trend; higher components = deviations
  • Only available when a Tucker3 model was used

Model comparison (from calibration) 

plot(fc, type = "model_comparison")
  • Same as plot(cal) but accessible from the forecast object
  • Useful when the calibration object is not retained

4. Standalone plotting functions

plot_forecast_trends()

Detailed trend plot with optional GAM credible intervals:

obs_dt    <- to_data_table(sm)
fc_dt     <- to_data_table(fc)
fitted_dt <- to_data_table(fc)  # fitted values

plot_forecast_trends(
  obs_dt         = obs_dt,
  fitted_dt      = fitted_dt,
  fc_dt          = fc_dt,
  output_dir     = tempdir(),
  cause_label    = "All causes",
  cause_short    = "all",
  forecast_years = 2021:2030,
  group_cols     = c("sex", "quintile")
)

plot_forecast_trends_by_age()

Fan charts faceted by selected age groups (40–44, 50–54, 60–64, 70–74, 80–84, 90+):

plot_forecast_trends_by_age(
  obs_dt         = obs_dt,
  fitted_dt      = fitted_dt,
  fc_dt          = fc_dt,
  output_dir     = tempdir(),
  cause_label    = "All causes",
  cause_short    = "all",
  forecast_years = 2021:2030
)

plot_forecast_age()

Age profile for the final forecast year, with PI bounds:

plot_forecast_age(
  fc_dt       = fc_dt,
  output_dir  = tempdir(),
  cause_label = "All causes",
  cause_short = "all",
  age_groups  = c("30-34", "35-39", "40-44", "45-49", "50-54",
                  "55-59", "60-64", "65-69", "70-74", "75-79",
                  "80-84", "85-89", "90+")
)

plot_obs_vs_smooth()

Detailed observed-vs-smoothed diagnostic:

plot_obs_vs_smooth(
  obs_dt      = obs_dt,
  smooth_dt   = to_data_table(sm),
  output_dir  = tempdir(),
  cause_label = "All causes",
  cause_short = "all"
)

plot_smoothing_comparison()

Raw vs smoothed scatter plot with COVID year highlighting:

plot_smoothing_comparison(
  mx_raw          = example_mortality$mx,
  mx_smooth       = sm$mx,
  years           = sm$years,
  ages            = sm$ages,
  output_dir      = tempdir(),
  cause_short     = "all",
  covid_years     = c(2020, 2021),
  floor_threshold = 1e-7
)

plot_B_components()

Tucker3 B-mode temporal components with forecast extensions:

plot_B_components(
  fc_obj         = fc$extras$full_fc,
  forecast_years = 2021:2030,
  sim_years      = sm$years,
  output_dir     = tempdir(),
  cause_label    = "All causes",
  cause_short    = "all"
)

plot_model_comparison()

Standalone model comparison bar chart:

plot_model_comparison(
  comp_dt     = cal$comparison,
  output_dir  = tempdir(),
  cause_label = "All causes",
  cause_short = "all"
)

5. Disaggregation diagnostic plots

plot_disaggregation()

Overview of disaggregated single-year mortality profiles:

plot_disaggregation(
  mx_1yr_dt   = fc_1yr$extras$mx_1yr_dt,
  output_dir  = tempdir(),
  cause_label = "All causes",
  cause_short = "all"
)

plot_disagg_comparison()

Side-by-side comparison of Hyman+Kannisto vs Natural+Gompertz:

plot_disagg_comparison(
  mx_grouped  = fc$mx_point[, 1, 1],
  age_starts  = fc$ages,
  target_ages = 30:100,
  output_dir  = tempdir(),
  cause_short = "all",
  width       = 5
)

plot_disagg_profile()

Detailed view of the GAM disaggregation stages — raw GAM prediction, parametric tail, blended result, and final corrected rates:

plot_disagg_profile(
  disagg      = fc_1yr$extras$disagg_obj,
  mx_grouped  = fc$mx_point[, 1, 1],
  ages        = fc$ages,
  width       = 5,
  fc_year_idx = 1L,
  group_idx   = 1L,
  open_mid    = 95,
  output_dir  = tempdir(),
  cause_short = "all",
  group_label = "Male Q1"
)

plot_disagg_smoothness()

Heatmap of second differences |Δ2log(mx)||\Delta^2 \log(m_x)| across groups and years, identifying kinks or discontinuities:

plot_disagg_smoothness(
  mx_1yr_dt   = fc_1yr$extras$mx_1yr_dt,
  output_dir  = tempdir(),
  cause_short = "all"
)

plot_disagg_temporal()

Temporal consistency at selected probe ages (50, 70, 85, 90, 95, 100):

plot_disagg_temporal(
  disagg         = fc_1yr$extras$disagg_obj,
  years          = sm$years,
  forecast_years = 2021:2030,
  group_idx      = 1L,
  output_dir     = tempdir(),
  cause_short    = "all",
  group_label    = "Male Q1",
  probe_ages     = c(50, 70, 85, 90, 95, 100)
)

plot_disagg_correction()

Bar chart of iterative group-mean correction factors:

plot_disagg_correction(
  disagg      = fc_1yr$extras$disagg_obj,
  mx_forecast = fc$mx_point,
  ages        = fc$ages,
  fc_year_idx = 1L,
  group_idx   = 1L,
  output_dir  = tempdir(),
  cause_short = "all",
  max_age     = 100
)

6. Multi-cause plots

plot_share_evolution()

Stacked area chart showing cause-of-death shares over time (observed + forecast):

plot_share_evolution(
  shares_obs_4d = shares_4d,
  shares_fc_4d  = fc_t4$shares_forecast,
  years_obs     = data_all$years,
  years_fc      = 2021:2030,
  disease_order = c("cancer", "cvd", "resp", "residual"),
  output_dir    = tempdir(),
  group_index   = 1,
  groups        = data_all$groups
)

plot_consistency_check()

Boxplot of ∑kmk/mall\sum_k m_k / m_{\text{all}} verifying that reconciled disease forecasts sum to all-cause:

plot_consistency_check(
  fc_dt_combined = combined_disease_dt,
  ac_fc_dt       = all_cause_dt,
  output_dir     = tempdir()
)

7. Colour palette

All model-comparison plots use a consistent colour scheme via model_colors():

cols <- model_colors()
print(cols)
# Tucker3-CoDa      Tucker3-Direct    Lee-Carter    FDM
# "#E41A1C"          "#377EB8"        "#4DAF4A"    "#984EA3"
# StMoMo-APC         ETS-Damped    ARIMA-perSeries   RWD
# "#FF7F00"          "#A65628"        "#F781BF"    "#999999"
# Ensemble
# "#000000"

Use these colours in custom ggplot2 plots for consistency:

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cal$comparison, aes(x = model, y = mase_combined, fill = model)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = model_colors()) +
  theme_minimal()

8. Output to files

All standalone plot_*() functions accept an output_dir parameter and save PNG files:

# All plots saved to a directory
output <- "publication_figures/"
dir.create(output, showWarnings = FALSE)

plot_model_comparison(cal$comparison, output, "All causes", "all")
plot_forecast_trends(obs_dt, fitted_dt, fc_dt, output, "All causes", "all",
                     forecast_years = 2021:2030)
plot_forecast_trends_by_age(obs_dt, fitted_dt, fc_dt, output, "All causes",
                            "all", forecast_years = 2021:2030)
plot_disaggregation(fc_1yr$extras$mx_1yr_dt, output, "All causes", "all")

File naming follows the convention: {cause_short}_{plot_type}.png.

Quick reference

Plot Function / Type Object Purpose
Heatmap plot(md, type="heatmap") mort_data Lexis surface
Age profile plot(md, type="age_profile") mort_data Age gradient
Trend plot(md, type="trend") mort_data Time series
Model comparison plot(cal) mort_calibration Model ranking
PI fan plot(fc, type="pi") mort_forecast Uncertainty
Trends + PI plot(fc, type="trends") mort_forecast Forecast trajectory
Age profiles plot(fc, type="age") mort_forecast Age shape
Residuals plot(fc, type="residuals") mort_forecast Model fit
Smoothing plot(fc, type="smoothing") mort_forecast Smooth quality
Components plot(fc, type="components") mort_forecast Tucker B-mode
Disaggregation plot_disaggregation() data.table Single-year profiles
Method comparison plot_disagg_comparison() arrays HK vs NG
Disagg profile plot_disagg_profile() disagg object GAM stages
Smoothness plot_disagg_smoothness() data.table Kink detection
Temporal plot_disagg_temporal() disagg object Age-year consistency
Corrections plot_disagg_correction() disagg object Group-mean factors
Share evolution plot_share_evolution() 4D arrays Cause shares
Consistency plot_consistency_check() data.tables Disease sum check
